findings.title: SQL injection via string interpolation in migration
findings.body: The host value `h` from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting is interpolated directly into the SQL INSERT statement without any sanitization or parameterization: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If a site admin had previously entered a malicious value into the `embeddable_hosts` setting (e.g., containing a single quote), this migration would execute arbitrary SQL. Use a parameterized query or at minimum `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`.

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting doesn't match any category
findings.body: The query `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` will return zero rows when the `embed_category` site setting is empty (its default) or doesn't match any category name. In that case, `execute(...)[0]` returns `nil`, and calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration. This will affect most sites since the default value of `embed_category` was an empty string. The nil check on line 14 (`if category_id == 0`) is never reached.

findings.title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil, inconsistent return type
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `false` on lines 12 and 15 when the URI is invalid or the host is blank, but returns an `EmbeddableHost` record or `nil` from the `where(...).first` call on line 17. Callers like `TopicEmbed.import` use `eh.try(:category_id)` which works with `false` (returns nil), but the method contract is broken: any caller that checks `result.nil?` or tries to use the return value as a record will behave incorrectly. The method should return `nil` consistently instead of `false`.

findings.title: before_validation callback crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` if `self.host` is nil. This can happen when `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create` is called with a missing or nil `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, since `save_host` assigns the param value to `host.host` before calling `save`, which triggers the callback. A guard like `self.host&.sub!` or a presence check is needed.

findings.title: destroy action raises NoMethodError when host not found
findings.body: In the `destroy` action, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` if no record matches. Calling `host.destroy` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`. The same issue exists in the `update` action (line 10-11) where `save_host(nil)` would crash when trying to assign attributes. Both actions should handle the not-found case, e.g., by using `find` (which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` and returns a 404) or by explicitly checking for nil.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped with their filenames
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. The file contents are swapped relative to their names. While Fabrication loads all files in the fabricators directory so tests may still pass, this is confusing for maintenance and could cause issues if fabricators are loaded selectively or if developers look for a fabricator by filename.

findings.title: _focusOnInput runs when editing becomes false, targeting a non-existent element
findings.body: The `_focusOnInput` method is triggered by `@observes('editing')` which fires whenever the `editing` property changes, including when it changes to `false` (e.g., after saving or cancelling). When `editing` is false, the `.host-name` input is not rendered, so `this.$('.host-name')` returns an empty jQuery object. While jQuery's `.focus()` on an empty set is a no-op, the intent is clearly to only focus when entering edit mode. Adding a guard like `if (this.get('editing'))` would make the behavior explicit and avoid unnecessary DOM queries.
